# Project log

## 2026-10-04 — Starship fleet and project organization

User requirements: a full-scale crewed Starship/Super Heavy fleet; small cargo behind visible side doors; large telescope/vehicles in an attached closing clamshell; a complete twin tower mount; strong precision-capable RCS; straight deployment and reduced wobbling; a Codex sidebar project; leave KSP open after checking.

Installed 49 craft: 24 side-door variants, 24 large clamshell variants, and one booster practice craft. Added custom controls and scaled 9 m hulls, engines, fuel systems, flaps, legs, and tower components. Four slow deployment pistons provide a straight 9.6 m travel and lock at the ends. Installed official KJR Next 4.2.28; its assembly and flight manager load were confirmed in KSP.log.

Added official Starship Launch Expansion 0.5 and Resurfaced 1.3.1. Added the six native cargo model/texture files from Tundra Exploration 5.1.0 for personal use, with the original asset license. The source assets remain unmodified; the custom nose hinge opens 110 degrees.

Static clearance: all 14 payload variants passed the 9.6 m deployment sweep against open bay meshes. These checks are geometric evidence, not proof of every possible orbital separation.

In-game checks in progress: fleet opening/extension/stowing, telescope orbital separation and automatic return stow, launch tower staging, and ship/booster landing hops. Do not treat any pending check as passed.

Project organization: source and guides copied into this folder. Sidebar registration is pending because the computer-use tool refuses com.openai.codex for safety reasons, and the Codex connector has no create-project action. A sidebar section is not a substitute for the requested project.

### Heavy cargo arm correction

The four-piston ground test failed: the telescope and distal arm parts detached and hit the launchpad during extension. Do not reuse that chain or describe its test as successful. Replaced it with one 4x telescoping actuator with the same folded payload position and 9.6 m travel. Native engage/disengage lock methods replace direct lock-field changes. Further live validation is pending.

The rescaled robotic model also failed during initialization: stock robotics gave the enlarged part an extension offset and the release collar collided. Replaced its geometry with the native large stock piston at scale 1, configured 9.6 m stroke, and a lightweight visual sleeve to cover the longer extension. The payload folded position remains unchanged. Further checks pending.

### Successful orbital deployment

The native-scale single actuator passed the telescope deployment at an inserted 150 km test orbit. All 36 flight parts remained intact through extension; the 11-part telescope separated with independent control; the carrier retained 25 parts and two crew, then automatically retracted, closed, and locked its nose. This is an inserted orbit test, not proof of launch to orbit or return.

The tower staging test released the mount and its arms, but the fully scaled booster engine thrust was overwritten by procedural engine-count settings. Scaled their singleEngineThrust and engine mass settings by 4.096. Full-fuel ascent test pending.

### Launch mount clearance correction

The first full-thrust run struck the folded booster legs against the mount at release and failed the two main structural connections. Widened the mount mesh horizontally by 1.65 while keeping tower positions and height unchanged, and strengthened the tank/engine/mount connections. Fresh ascent and separation validation pending.

### Native actuator, crew clearance, and screenshots

The final native-scale single actuator passed ground extension and return stow with the Hubble payload: 49 parts intact, two carrier crew, fully extended locked actuator, then closed/locked nose. Moved and reduced the permanent cabin to a rear bay position; both cabin and telescope are shielded when closed. All 14 payload bounding volumes are separate from the cabin, and their outward deployment increases separation.

Low-resolution reflections restore visibility of reflective materials; previous performance settings had reflections disabled. Taking a labelled photo album of every mission payload and major visible change. The album uses actual game captures and records craft, part count, crew, time, and test conditions.

### Cargo staging correction

The surface-base parachutes added an extra stage. Disabled native staging for payload parachutes, preserving the same two-step booster launch/ship separation order. Payload key 5 deploys parachutes through a guarded action only after separation; while aboard Starship, key 5 remains the carrier flap preset. Fresh loaded staging and separation checks pending.

### Final fleet and functional checks

All 16 final Full Stacks fresh-loaded at launch stage 2 with payload engines off. Disabling staging fields in craft files alone did not prevent an extra stage. Separate non-staged Spark/Poodle/parachute prefabs preserve the stock model geometry; all three cloned meshes match their originals.

Full-fuel Empty Tower Launch passed with 36 flight parts after the arms cleared, then 25 ship parts and two crew after separation. The 11-part booster could be selected and put in landing-engine mode. The nine-part ground launcher has a powered control point; switching back, closing its native arms and reopening them passed.

The final surface-base craft passed deployment in an inserted 150 km test orbit with all 44 flight parts. Its engine and parachute commands stayed blocked aboard the carrier. The 19-part payload separated, then its engine activation/shutdown, parachute arming and equipment controls worked. The carrier retained 25 parts and two crew, automatically retracted, closed and locked. This does not test a base landing.

Starship practice at 20 percent fuel landed with 25 parts and two crew after observed airborne telemetry above 219 m radar altitude. The first monitor stopped at an initial release bounce; later telemetry separately records the flight and touchdown, so a complete maximum-altitude trace is unavailable. Booster practice at 5 percent fuel reached 214.74 m and landed with all 11 parts. These are pad-area hops, not orbital recovery.

All 14 payloads passed the mesh sweep and cabin-volume checks. The final 16 extended snapshots measured at most 0.218 degrees of release-collar deviation from the actuator axis. Four ship legs, leg lock, flap preset, and high/precision hull RCS controls passed.

Photo delivery: 60 actual game captures cover all 16 cargo designs and the major visible changes. The PDF and searchable HTML preserve original PNGs. Backlit inserted-orbit captures are being replaced with lit-side views; the safe parked Hubble tower craft is saved before that final photo session.

Limits: launch-to-orbit, full re-entry/return to launch site, belly-flop/flip, docking, Mun/Duna delivery, long-duration crew operations, and automatic catching have not been flown. Automatic catching is not implemented. No FPS benchmark was run. Sidebar project registration remains pending due to the Codex app control restriction.

### Intermittent separation contact found during photo retakes

The second surface-base orbital run lost the release collar and one landing leg after separation (carrier 24, payload 18), although the previous run passed. Preserved the failure save and telemetry. This means the earlier pass alone was insufficient.

Added a temporary collision guard only between the deployment hardware (arm/collar) and the released cargo. Native collision handling changes when one vessel becomes two; the failure log records collar/leg explosions and the habitat leaving contact with capTransform; support and folded payload bounds overlap. The guard keeps those support contacts disabled until their bounds separate, then restores them. Cargo-bay wall collisions remain active. Repeating separation validation before final acceptance.

### Separation guard passed; external fixture clearance

Repeated the original surface-base failure profile with attitude hold off. All 44 flight parts remained through deployment, then 19 payload parts and 25 carrier parts survived. Both carrier crew remained. The guard assigned 342 support/cargo collider pairs and released all of them after withdrawal; the nose closed and locked. Independent engine, equipment and parachute controls passed.

A direct daylight orbit insertion on the pad loaded only 42 parts: the dome light and telescoping ladder were lost before deployment. Preserved setup-damage telemetry and its save separately. Moved the lamp to the main tank exterior and the ladder farther out from the skin, then regenerated all 49 crafts. This changes external fixture placement without changing payloads, joints, mass, engines or staging. Testing the same direct orbit insertion and photographing the new clearance.

### Finished validation and photo delivery

The final fixture placement passed the direct daylight orbit insertion with all 44 parts, then the full surface-base release and control handoff with 19 payload/25 carrier parts and both carrier crew. The final telescope also passed with 36 parts through deployment, 11 independently controlled payload parts and 25 carrier parts/two crew after automatic retraction, nose closing and lock. Its support-contact guards cleared after withdrawal.

63 curated actual screenshots show all 16 mission designs, cargo opening/extension/stow, tower assemblies and staging, independent booster/tower control, ship/booster landing legs, RCS modes, graphics comparison, orbital payloads and the two hull fixture adjustments. Original PNGs, captions and telemetry are preserved; composition previews and misnamed duplicate captures are excluded from the album and retained separately.

Compiled and installed the normal plugin without TestBridge. Disabled the development flag so the running bridge destroys itself. KSP remains open on the final 56-part Hubble Tower Launch craft, safely parked with two crew, manual throttle at zero and cargo closed. Native U lighting was checked and the ready state saved with F5. The original save 987 is untouched.

All 49 installed craft match the generated copies. Source, current settings, clean installed custom-mod snapshot, guides, evidence, PDF and searchable HTML are gathered here. The only organizational handoff is selecting this folder through Codex Add project; automatic sidebar registration is blocked by the app control restriction. Full orbital recovery, docking, Mun/Duna operations and automatic tower catching remain unflown; catching is not implemented.

Album QA completed: 63 PDF pages, representative pages visually inspected,
all captions fit, page numbering checked, and all 63 gallery PNG paths resolve.
Final source/craft/mod/settings/photo copies were synchronized; installed craft
bytes match all 49 project copies. KSP process was verified running.
